qc.label_under_test: Weak, dense hum that rises on a word NAMING the mental-health field or its professions (psychiatrist, psychiatric, psychiatry, psychologist, psychology, psychoanalysis, 'mental health'), even with no treatment in the scene (a research psychologist studying memory ~0.5). Mental-health care described without such a word stays low (ward doses of clozapine and lithium ~0.14, the same as insulin; inpatient anorexia clinic ~0.12), as do psych- lookalikes ('psychic', the film 'Psycho'); the same sentence with 'doctor' instead of 'psychiatrist' drops from ~0.46 to ~0.14. Known side channels kept from the earlier label: the '-therapy' family (speech therapy ~0.46), ' talking' and the 'Too Little too Late?' headline. Of its newly mapped neighbours only L8/N2771+ (weight-loss surgery) is medical: after a gastric bypass, 'referred to a psychologist' ~0.65, 'referred to a surgeon' ~0.17.

neighbours.label: Weak, dense hum that rises on mental-health care vocabulary: words naming the field or its professions (psychiatrist, psychiatric, psychologist, psychology, 'mental health') and words for talking-cure care (therapy, talk therapy, counselling, sharing feelings in group sessions). Plain diagnoses (depression, anxiety) and therapy acronyms (CBT) stay low. Known side channel: the word ' talking' even outside care (a talking parrot ~0.3); ordinary medical scenes hum at 0.1-0.4, so it is a weak preference, not a clean switch.
